passages.source_text: Ἐγὼ Κλήμης, Ῥωμαίων πολίτης ὢν, καὶ τὴν πρώτην ἡλικίαν σωφρόνως ζῆσαι δεδύνημαι, τῆς ἐννοίας μου ἐκ παιδὸς ἀπασχολούσης τὴν ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐπιθυμίαν εἴς τε ἀθυμίας καὶ πόνους. συνῆν γάρ μοι λογισμὸς (οὐκ οἶδα πόθεν τὴν ἀρχὴν λαβών) περὶ θανάτου, πυκνὰς ποιούμενος ὑπομνήσεις ὅτι ἄρα θανὼν οὐκ εἰμὶ καὶ οὐδὲ μνήμην τις ποιήσει μού ποτε, τοῦ ἀπείρου χρόνου πάντων τὰ πάντα εἰς λήθην φέροντος — ἔσομαι δὲ οὐκ ὤν, οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς, οὐ γινώσκων, οὐ γινωσκόμενος, οὐ γεγονώς, οὐ γινόμενος — καὶ ἆρά ποτε γέγονεν ὁ κόσμος καὶ πρὸ τοῦ γενέσθαι τί ἄρα ἦν (εἰ γὰρ ἦν ἀεί, καὶ ἔσται· εἰ δὲ γέγονεν, καὶ λυθήσεται) καὶ μετὰ λύσιν τί ἄρα ἔσται πάλιν, εἰ μὴ τάχα σιγὴ καὶ λήθη; καὶ τάχα ἔσται τι ὃ νῦν νοῆσαι οὐ δυνατόν.

ταῦτά τε καὶ τὰ τούτοις ὅμοια οὐκ οἶδα πόθεν ἀπαύστως ἐνθυμούμενος ὀδυνηρὰν εἶχον λύπην τοσοῦτον ὡς ὠχριακότα με τήκεσθαι· καὶ τὸ δεινότατον, εἴ ποτε ἀπώσασθαι τὴν φροντίδα ὡς ἀνωφελῆ ἐβουλευσάμην, ἀκμαιότερόν μοι μᾶλλον τὸ πάθος ἐγίνετο. καὶ ἠχθόμην ἐπὶ τούτῳ, οὐκ εἰδὼς σύνοικον καλὴν ἔχων ἔννοιαν, ἀθανασίας ἀγαθῆς αἰτίαν μοι γενησομένην, ὡς ὕστερον τῇ πείρᾳ ἐπέγνων καὶ θεῷ τῷ πάντων δεσπότῃ ηὐχαρίστησα. ὑπὸ γὰρ τῆς κατ᾽ ἀρχὰς θλιβούσης με ἐννοίας εἰς τὴν τῶν πραγμάτων ζήτησιν καὶ εὕρεσιν ἠναγκάσθην ἐλθεῖν· καὶ τότε ἐταλάνιζον οὓς τὴν ἀρχὴν διὰ ἄγνοιαν μακαρίζειν ἐκινδύνευον.

ἐκ παιδὸς οὖν ἡλικίας ὢν ἐν τοιούτοις λογισμοῖς, χάριν τοῦ μαθεῖν τι βέβαιον εἰς τὰς τῶν φιλοσόφων ἐφοίτων διατριβάς. καὶ οὐδὲν ἕτερον εὕρων ἢ δογμάτων ἀνασκευὰς καὶ κατασκευὰς καὶ ἔρεις καὶ φιλονεικίας καὶ συλλογισμῶν τέχνας καὶ λημμάτων ἐπινοίας. καὶ ὁτὲ μὲν ἐπεκράτει (φέρε λέγειν) ὅτι ἀθάνατος ἡ ψυχή, ὁτὲ δὲ ὅτι θνητή. εἴ ποτε οὖν ἐπεκράτει λόγος ὅτι ἀθάνατος, ἔχαιρον· ὁπότε δὲ ὅτι θνητή, ἐλυπούμην. πλεῖον δὲ ἠθύμουν ὅτι οὐδ᾽ ὁπότερον εἰς τὸν ἐμὸν βεβαιῶσαι νοῦν ἠδυνάμην. πλὴν συνένοουν ὅτι αἱ δόξαι τῶν ὑποθέσεων παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας ψευδεῖς ἢ ἀληθεῖς ὑπολαμβάνονται καὶ οὐχ ὡς ἔχουσιν ἀληθείας φαίνονται. ἐπιστήσας οὖν ἤδη ποτὲ ὅτι οὐ παρὰ τὰς ἐκδικουμένας ὑποθέσεις ἡ κατάληψις γίνεται, ἀλλὰ παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας αἱ δόξαι ἀποφαίνονται, ἔτι μᾶλλον ἰλιγγίων ἐν τοῖς πράγμασιν. διὸ ἐκ τοῦ τῆς ψυχῆς βάθους ἐστέναζον· οὔτε γάρ τι βεβαιῶσαι οἷός τ᾽ ἤμην οὐδὲ τὴν τῶν τοιούτων φροντίδα ἀποσείσασθαι ἐδυνάμην, καίπερ βουλόμενος, ὡς φθάσας εἶπον· ὅτι ἐμαυτῷ πυκνότερον ἡσυχάζειν ἐπιτάσσοντος, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅπως λανθανόντως μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς ὁ τῶν τοιούτων μοι εἰσήρχετο λογισμός.

καὶ πάλιν ἀπορούμενος ἔλεγον ἐμαυτῷ Τί ματαιοπονῶ; σαφοῦς ὄντος τοῦ πράγματος ὅτι εἰ μὲν θανὼν οὐκ εἰμί, νῦν ὄντα με λυπεῖσθαι οὐ προσῆκεν. διὸ τηρήσω τὸ λυπεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν τότε, ὅτε οὐκ ὢν οὐ λυπηθήσομαι. εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα εἰμί τι, νῦν ἐκ περισσοῦ μοι πρόσεστιν τὸ λυπεῖσθαι. καὶ εὐθέως μετὰ τοῦτο ἕτερός με εἰσήει λογισμός· ἔλεγον γὰρ Εἰ μήτι γε τοῦ νῦν με λυποῦντος ἐκεῖ χεῖρον παθεῖν ἔχω, μὴ βεβιωκὼς εὐσεβῶς, καὶ παραδοθήσομαι κατ’ ἐνίων φιλοσόφων λόγους Πυριφλεγέθοντι καὶ Ταρτάρῳ ὡς Σίσυφος ἢ Τιτυὸς ἢ Ἰξίων ἢ Τάνταλος, καὶ ἔσομαι ἐν ᾅδου τὸν αἰῶνα κολαζόμενος. πάλιν τε ἀνθυπέφερον λέγων Ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἔστιν ταῦτα. καὶ πάλιν ἔλεγον Εἰ δὲ ἔστιν; ἀδήλου οὖν ὄντος τοῦ πράγματος (ἔλεγον) ἀκινδυνότερόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον εὐσεβῶς βιῶσαί με. καὶ πῶς δυνήσομαι, τοῦ δικαίου χάριν εἰς ἄδηλον ἐλπίδα ἀφορῶν, τῶν τοῦ σώματος κρατεῖν ἡδονῶν; ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ τί ποτε ἔστιν δίκαιον ἀρέσκον θεῷ πεπληροφόρημαι οὔτε εἰ ἡ ψυχὴ ἀθάνατος ἢ θνητὴ γινώσκω οὔτε τίς λόγος βέβαιος εὑρίσκεται, οὔτε τῶν τοιούτων λογισμῶν ἡσυχάζειν δύναμαι.

context.translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | reorient / reorientation; toward God where the context warrants making the destination explicit | repent / repentance (traditional); reconsider / change of mind in documented exceptions | See "Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)" below; do not homogenize regret, divine relenting, or distinct turning words |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.

passages.text: I, Clement, am a Roman citizen, and I have been able to live my early life with self-control, because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied with dejection and distress. For a thought about death stayed with me—I do not know where it began—repeatedly reminding me that, once dead, I do not exist and no one will ever remember me, as infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion. I shall be nonexistent, knowing those who do not exist, not knowing, not being known, not having come into being, not coming into being. And has the world ever come into being? Before it came into being, what was there? For if it has always existed, it will also exist; but if it came into being, it will also be dissolved. And after its dissolution, what will there be in turn, unless perhaps silence and oblivion? Perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived.

lexical_decisions.chosen: am a Roman citizen
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses the conventional English description while preserving Clement’s stated civic identity.

lexical_decisions.chosen: live my early life with self-control
lexical_decisions.rationale: σωφρόνως denotes restrained or temperate conduct, while πρώτη ἡλικία refers to the earliest period of life.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς ἐννοίας μου ἐκ παιδὸς ἀπασχολούσης τὴν ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐπιθυμίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the causal force of the genitive absolute and the image of desire being kept occupied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ ἀπείρου χρόνου πάντων τὰ πάντα εἰς λήθην φέροντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: as infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains both the personification of time and the emphatic πάντων τὰ πάντα.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ τάχα ἔσται τι ὃ νῦν νοῆσαι οὐ δυνατόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived
lexical_decisions.rationale: νοῆσαι concerns mental conception or apprehension, not merely physical perception.

source_issues.source_quote: ἔσομαι δὲ οὐκ ὤν, οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς
source_issues.issue: The supplied masculine plural οὐκ ὄντας has no explicit antecedent. It can be construed as the object of εἰδώς, yielding the unusual sense “knowing those who do not exist,” but the intended relation to the surrounding catalogue of nonexistence remains uncertain.

passages.text: Constantly pondering these and similar things—I do not know from where—I had such painful grief that I grew pale and wasted away. Worst of all, if I ever resolved to thrust the concern away as useless, the affliction became all the more acute for me. I was distressed at this, not knowing that I had a beautiful thought as a housemate, one that would become for me the cause of a good immortality, as I later learned by experience and thanked God, the Master of all. For by the thought that distressed me at first, I was compelled to come to the investigation and discovery of realities; and then I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of pronouncing blessed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: constantly pondering
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys both the uninterrupted recurrence and the inwardly reflective character of ἐνθυμέομαι.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀκμαιότερόν μοι μᾶλλον τὸ πάθος ἐγίνετο
lexical_decisions.chosen: the affliction became all the more acute for me
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀκμαιότερον describes the condition as growing stronger or more intense.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I had a beautiful thought as a housemate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the domestic image of the thought dwelling together with Clement.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the cause of a good immortality
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the explicit qualification ἀγαθῆς, which may distinguish beneficial immortality from an enduring state of punishment.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐταλάνιζον οὓς τὴν ἀρχὴν διὰ ἄγνοιαν μακαρίζειν ἐκινδύνευον
lexical_decisions.chosen: I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of pronouncing blessed
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the deliberate opposition between ταλανίζω and μακαρίζω.

passages.text: From childhood, then, while occupied with such thoughts, I frequented the philosophers’ schools in order to learn something certain. I found nothing else there but doctrines being torn down and built up, disputes and rivalries, techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises. At one time, for example, the position that the soul is immortal prevailed; at another, the position that it is mortal. Whenever an argument that it was immortal prevailed, I rejoiced; but whenever one that it was mortal prevailed, I grieved. Yet I was more disheartened because I was unable to establish either alternative as certain in my own mind. Still, I understood that opinions about the theses are taken as false or true according to those who defend them and do not appear as they actually stand with respect to truth. Having therefore at last recognized that a firm grasp is not attained on the basis of the theses being defended, but that opinions are pronounced on the basis of those defending them, and reeling still more amid these matters, I groaned from the depth of my soul. For I was neither able to establish anything as certain, nor could I shake off concern for such matters, although I wanted to, as I said earlier; for when I kept ordering myself to be still, I do not know how, the thought of such things would enter me unnoticed and with pleasure.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὰς τῶν φιλοσόφων ἐφοίτων διατριβάς
lexical_decisions.chosen: I frequented the philosophers’ schools
lexical_decisions.rationale: διατριβαί here denotes places or circles of philosophical instruction rather than casual conversation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: doctrines being torn down and built up
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the paired constructive and destructive imagery rather than reducing it to generic disagreement.

lexical_decisions.chosen: techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises
lexical_decisions.rationale: λήμματα are propositions or premises adopted in argument, while τέχναι emphasizes methodical argumentative techniques.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αἱ δόξαι τῶν ὑποθέσεων παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας ψευδεῖς ἢ ἀληθεῖς ὑπολαμβάνονται
lexical_decisions.chosen: opinions about the theses are taken as false or true according to those who defend them
lexical_decisions.rationale: παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας makes the advocates, rather than the intrinsic merits of the theses, the basis of the assessment.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ παρὰ τὰς ἐκδικουμένας ὑποθέσεις ἡ κατάληψις γίνεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: a firm grasp is not attained on the basis of the theses being defended
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατάληψις is used in a philosophical context for apprehension or secure cognitive grasp.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: λανθανόντως μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς ὁ τῶν τοιούτων μοι εἰσήρχετο λογισμός
lexical_decisions.chosen: the thought of such things would enter me unnoticed and with pleasure
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps both the stealth conveyed by λανθανόντως and the expressly pleasurable quality conveyed by μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς.

passages.text: Again, at a loss, I said to myself, “Why am I laboring in vain? The matter is clear: if, once dead, I do not exist, it is not fitting for me to grieve while I now exist. Therefore I will reserve grieving for that time, when, since I will not exist, I will not grieve. But if, after all, I do exist in some way, then my grieving now is superfluous.” Immediately after this, another thought entered me, for I said, “What if, indeed, because I have not lived devoutly, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now, and according to the accounts of certain philosophers I shall be handed over to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus, like Sisyphus or Tityus or Ixion or Tantalus, and shall be in Hades, punished for all time?” Again I countered, saying, “But these things are not real.” And again I said, “But what if they are? Since the matter is uncertain, then, it is safer for me to live devoutly instead. Yet how will I be able, for the sake of what is right, while looking toward an uncertain hope, to master the pleasures of the body? But I have not even been fully assured of what exactly is right and pleasing to God; nor do I know whether the soul is immortal or mortal, nor what reliable account can be found, nor am I able to rest from such thoughts.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: Why am I laboring in vain?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the image of expending effort fruitlessly.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τηρήσω τὸ λυπεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν τότε
lexical_decisions.chosen: I will reserve grieving for that time
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats τὴν τότε as an elliptical expression for the future time under discussion without supplying it as Greek text.

lexical_decisions.chosen: if, after all, I do exist in some way
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the deliberately indefinite τι while expressing the implied question of existence after death.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Εἰ μήτι γε τοῦ νῦν με λυποῦντος ἐκεῖ χεῖρον παθεῖν ἔχω
lexical_decisions.chosen: What if, indeed, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders εἰ μήτι γε as an apprehensive possibility arising against Clement’s preceding reassurance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus
lexical_decisions.rationale: Transliterates the named mythological places rather than replacing them with generalized terms.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in Hades, punished for all time
lexical_decisions.rationale: The accusative duration τὸν αἰῶνα presents the punishment as indefinitely or perpetually enduring.

lexical_decisions.chosen: for the sake of what is right
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantivized neuter refers to right conduct rather than necessarily invoking a technical doctrine of righteousness.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what reliable account can be found
lexical_decisions.rationale: λόγος may denote an argument or account here; “account” leaves that scope open while βέβαιος conveys dependability.

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.
